title: optimize cpu request path: reduce serialization overhead, thread-pool refactor, and core pinning
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: CPU-side work in the request path (serialization, per-request bookkeeping, tokenization handoffs, and thread-pool scheduling) was a measurable contributor to end-to-end latency and increased tail latencies under bursty traffic. This PR targets three classes of CPU-side bottlenecks: 1) high-overhead serialization/deserialization between internal protobuf objects and JSON for logging/metrics, 2) contention and suboptimal sizing in the request thread pools, and 3) OS scheduler jitter for hot inference worker threads. Summary of changes: - Replace hot-path protobuf->JSON conversions with a lightweight, preallocated header+field serializer for routing/metrics when full JSON is not required. This removes heap allocations in the common case and batches stats emission.
- Introduce a per-NUMA worker thread-pool (RequestWorkerPool) with configurable shard_count and a lock-free work-queue for low-latency dispatch. The pool defaults to #cores/2 and is pinned to a core-set derived from the runtime's cpu_affinity config.
- Add optional CPU affinity pinning (config runtime.cpu_affinity.mode = "balanced" | "compact" | "none") with a conservative default of "balanced" on Dedicated and Private. Pinning is no-op on environments where affinity isn't supported.
- Reduce coarse-grained locks in the request router by using atomic sequence counters for request ids and a small object-pool for per-request context structs to avoid per-request malloc/free churn.
- Move tokenization and prompt preprocessing off the main acceptor thread onto the worker-pool; introduce a fast-path for short requests (< 512 tokens) that avoids copying the token buffer when the tokenizer is single-pass.
- Add integration + perf tests (canary harness) and a deterministic scheduler test that reproduces the previous tail-latency regression. Testing and CI: - Local perf harness: p50 latency down ~16%, p95 down ~28% on medium-sized Llama-like model config under bursty-concurrent workload (N=64 concurrent requests) with throughput improvement ~12% in sustained load tests.
- Unit/Integration: new RequestWorkerPool unit tests, deterministic scheduler test added to sched_tests.
- CI initially failed in sched_tests due to a flaky timing assumption; fixed by replacing wall-clock sleeps with condition-variable waits tied to test hooks.
- All checks green on retry. Rollout and migration notes: - Feature gated under runtime.feature_flags.cpu_request_optimize (off by default).
- Can be enabled progressively via canary: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic fallback to baseline if CPU p95 increases by >10% vs baseline.
- No model changes required. Backwards compatibility: non-breaking. See release_notes for recommended toggle guidance. Related: Linear ENG-1792, ENG-1820.

release_notes: CPU request-path optimizations: lower p50/p95 latency and improved throughput via lightweight serialization, per-NUMA worker pools, and optional CPU affinity pinning. Feature gated; enable via runtime.feature_flags.cpu_request_optimize. See docs/ops/canary_playbook.md for rollout steps.
perf_results: Local canary harness: p50 -16% latency, p95 -28% latency on bursty workload (64 concurrent), sustained throughput +12%. Deterministic scheduler test eliminates prior tail variance.
notes_on_rollout: Ship behind feature flag. Start at 5% traffic, monitor CPU p95 and request success rate. Fallback automatically if regressions detected. For Dedicated/Private, default cpu_affinity.mode is 'balanced'.
